What this tutorial is for

This page is a quick tour of sharkipediaR — not the full package manual (that lives on the home page and in Reference).

Sharkipedia holds published shark and ray traits and population trends. This package pulls that into R as tidy tables you can filter and plot.

Load the package 

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
library(sharkipediaR)

Three commands worth knowing

When you are online, almost everything starts here:

sp_species("Carcharodon carcharias")   # taxonomy
sp_traits("Carcharodon carcharias")    # life-history table
sp_trends("Carcharodon carcharias")      # abundance through time

Each result includes source_url and retrieved_at — keep them for methods sections and supplementary files.

Try it without the internet

Vignettes use frozen data so GitHub Actions can build the site:

ex <- example_carcharhinus()
glimpse(ex$traits)
#> Rows: 39
#> Columns: 11
#> $ trait_name   <chr> "Direct Predation", "Direct Predation", "Amat50", "Gestat…
#> $ value        <chr> "Medium", "Medium", "4.3", "11", "15.51", "35.35", "28.83…
#> $ standard     <chr> "Effect size", "Strength of evidence", "Year", "Month", "…
#> $ value_type   <chr> "mean", "mean", "mean", "mean", "mean", "mean", "mean", "…
#> $ sex          <chr> "Pooled", "Pooled", "Male", "Female", "Female", "Female",…
#> $ location     <chr> "Caribbean", "Caribbean", "South Carolina", "South Caroli…
#> $ reference    <chr> "clementi2021", "clementi2021", "driggers2004a", "drigger…
#> $ trait_group  <chr> "Ecological Role", "Ecological Role", "Age", "Reproductio…
#> $ species      <chr> "Carcharhinus acronotus", "Carcharhinus acronotus", "Carc…
#> $ source_url   <chr> "https://www.sharkipedia.org/species/carcharhinus-acronot…
#> $ retrieved_at <dttm> 2026-05-25 12:00:00, 2026-05-25 12:00:00, 2026-05-25 12:…

For trend examples in the next tutorial, see example_reid2011_trends() and example_white_shark_trends().
